broad-bean.store: In their pods in the fridge for a few days; they're sweetest picked young.
broad-bean.preserve: Pod, blanch for two minutes and freeze.
broad-bean.use: Young ones raw with pecorino; bigger ones slipped from their grey skins after cooking.

runner-bean.store: In a bag in the fridge for up to five days.
runner-bean.preserve: Slice, blanch for two minutes and freeze, or make runner bean chutney.
runner-bean.use: Sliced thin on the slant, boiled briefly and buttered.

french-bean.store: In a bag in the fridge for up to five days.
french-bean.preserve: Blanch whole for two minutes and freeze.
french-bean.use: Steamed and dressed while warm, or in a salad with potatoes and egg.

pea.store: In their pods in the fridge, and eat within a day or two: the sugar turns to starch.
pea.preserve: Pod, blanch for a minute and freeze straight away.
pea.use: Raw from the pod, or cooked for two minutes with mint.

potato.store: Dry the skins for a few hours, then keep in paper sacks somewhere cool, dark and frost-free for months.
potato.preserve: Earlies don't keep: eat them. Maincrops keep until spring in the dark.
potato.use: New potatoes boiled with mint; maincrops for roasting, mash and chips.

onion.store: Dry in the sun for a fortnight, then hang in nets or plaits somewhere cool and airy for months.
onion.preserve: Pickle the small ones; slice and freeze the rest for cooking.
onion.use: The start of almost everything: slow-cooked until sweet.

shallot.store: Dry well, then keep in a cool, airy place until spring.
shallot.use: Roasted whole, or finely chopped in dressings.

garlic.store: Dry for two weeks, then plait or hang somewhere cool and airy for months.
garlic.preserve: Peel and keep in the freezer, or roast whole and freeze the soft cloves.
garlic.use: Fresh green garlic in early summer; dried bulbs all year.

leek.store: Leave them in the ground until you need them; they stand all winter.
leek.preserve: Wash, slice and freeze for soups.
leek.use: Melted slowly in butter, or in leek and potato soup.

spring-onion.store: In a glass of water in the fridge for a week.
spring-onion.use: Raw in salads, or charred whole on the griddle.

carrot.store: Twist off the tops; keep in the fridge for weeks, or in damp sand in a cool shed all winter.
carrot.preserve: Blanch and freeze, or pickle with cumin.
carrot.use: Raw and crunchy, roasted with honey, or in a soup with ginger.

parsnip.store: Leave them in the ground until you need them: frost makes them sweeter.
parsnip.preserve: Par-boil, roast lightly and freeze for quick roasts.
parsnip.use: Roasted until the edges catch, or in a spiced soup.

beetroot.store: Twist off the leaves; keep in the fridge for weeks, or in damp sand all winter.
beetroot.preserve: Pickle in vinegar, or cook and freeze.
beetroot.use: Roasted in foil, grated raw with apple, or in a chocolate cake.

radish.store: Tops off, in the fridge for a week.
radish.preserve: Quick-pickle in rice vinegar for a few days.
radish.use: Raw with butter and salt, or roasted for a gentler bite.

turnip.store: Tops off, in the fridge for a couple of weeks.
turnip.preserve: Cube, blanch and freeze for stews.
turnip.use: Small ones glazed in butter; the tops cook like greens.

lettuce.store: Pick in the cool of the morning; keep in a bag in the fridge for a few days.
lettuce.preserve: Doesn't keep: eat it fresh, a little and often.
lettuce.use: Salads, or the hearts halved and griddled.

spinach.store: In a bag in the fridge for two or three days.
spinach.preserve: Wilt, squeeze out the water and freeze in balls.
spinach.use: Raw when young, wilted with garlic when bigger.

chard.store: Stems in a glass of water in the fridge for a few days.
chard.preserve: Blanch the leaves and freeze; the stems are best fresh.
chard.use: Stems cooked first, leaves wilted in at the end.

kale.store: Pick leaves as you need them; in the fridge they keep for five days.
kale.preserve: Strip from the stalks, blanch and freeze.
kale.use: Crisped in the oven, or stirred through soups and pasta.

cabbage.store: Whole heads keep for weeks in the fridge or a cold shed.
cabbage.preserve: Make sauerkraut, or shred, blanch and freeze.
cabbage.use: Shredded thin for slaw, or braised slowly with apple.

sprouting-broccoli.store: In the fridge for a few days; keep picking and more will come.
sprouting-broccoli.preserve: Blanch for two minutes and freeze.
sprouting-broccoli.use: Steamed, with anchovy butter or lemon and chilli.

calabrese.store: In the fridge for up to a week.
calabrese.preserve: Cut into florets, blanch and freeze.
calabrese.use: Steamed, roasted until charred, or in a stir-fry.

cauliflower.store: In the fridge for a week, wrapped.
cauliflower.preserve: Blanch florets and freeze, or pickle in piccalilli.
cauliflower.use: Roasted whole with spices, or cauliflower cheese.

brussels-sprout.store: On the stalk somewhere cool for a couple of weeks.
brussels-sprout.use: Halved and fried hard with bacon or chestnuts.

courgette.store: In the fridge for up to a week; pick them small.
courgette.preserve: Grate and freeze for baking, or make courgette chutney.
courgette.use: Ribboned raw, griddled, or grated into a cake.

winter-squash.store: Cure in the sun for ten days, then keep somewhere warm and dry for months.
winter-squash.preserve: Roast and freeze the flesh, or make soup and freeze it.
winter-squash.use: Roasted in wedges, or soup with sage.

cucumber.store: At room temperature for a few days, or the fridge for a week.
cucumber.preserve: Pickle the small ones with dill.

tomato.store: At room temperature, out of the sun: the fridge dulls the flavour.
tomato.preserve: Roast and freeze as sauce; make green tomato chutney with the last of them.
tomato.use: Raw with salt and oil, or slow-roasted until jammy.

sweetcorn.store: Eat it the day you pick it: the sugar turns to starch within hours.
sweetcorn.preserve: Cut the kernels off and freeze.
sweetcorn.use: Boiled for four minutes and buttered, or grilled in the husk.

chilli.store: In the fridge for a couple of weeks.
chilli.preserve: Thread and dry, freeze whole, or make chilli jam.
chilli.use: Fresh in salsas and stir-fries; dried for winter cooking.

rocket.store: In a bag in the fridge for a few days.
rocket.preserve: Doesn't keep: make pesto and freeze it.
rocket.use: In salads, on pizza, or blitzed into pesto.

pak-choi.store: In the fridge for up to five days.
pak-choi.use: Halved and steamed with soy, or in a stir-fry.

kohlrabi.store: Leaves off, in the fridge for a couple of weeks.

swede.store: In a cool shed for months, or leave in the ground.
swede.use: Mashed with carrot and lots of pepper.

celeriac.store: Leave in the ground with straw over it, or keep in a cool shed for months.
celeriac.preserve: Cook and freeze as mash or soup.
celeriac.use: Remoulade raw, or roasted, or mashed with potato.

celery.store: In the fridge, wrapped, for a couple of weeks.
celery.preserve: Chop and freeze for soups and stews.
celery.use: Raw and crisp, or the base of a stock.

sweet-pepper.store: In the fridge for a week or so.
sweet-pepper.preserve: Roast, peel and freeze, or keep in oil in the fridge.
sweet-pepper.use: Roasted until soft and sweet, or raw in salads.

aubergine.store: At cool room temperature for a few days.
aubergine.preserve: Grill slices and freeze, or make a chutney.
aubergine.use: Roasted until silky, in baba ghanoush or a curry.

asparagus.store: Stand in water in the fridge, and eat within a day or two.
asparagus.preserve: Blanch and freeze, though it's best fresh.
asparagus.use: Steamed or griddled for a few minutes, with butter or a soft egg.

globe-artichoke.store: In the fridge for a few days.
globe-artichoke.preserve: Prepare the hearts and keep in oil in the fridge.
globe-artichoke.use: Boiled whole, leaves dipped in butter.

corn-salad.store: In a bag in the fridge for a few days.
corn-salad.use: A soft, nutty winter salad leaf.

mizuna.store: In a bag in the fridge for a few days.
mizuna.use: Peppery in salads, or wilted into noodle soups.

jerusalem-artichoke.store: Leave in the ground and dig as needed through winter.
jerusalem-artichoke.use: Roasted, or a silky soup. Go gently: they can be windy.

sweet-potato.store: Cure somewhere warm for a week, then keep at room temperature.
sweet-potato.use: Roasted, mashed, or in a curry.

florence-fennel.store: In the fridge for a week.
florence-fennel.preserve: Best fresh, though it can be braised and frozen.
florence-fennel.use: Shaved raw with orange, or braised until soft.

salsify.store: Leave in the ground and lift as needed.
salsify.use: Peeled, boiled and fried in butter.

pumpkin.store: Cure in the sun, then keep somewhere warm and dry for months.
pumpkin.preserve: Roast and freeze, or freeze as soup.
pumpkin.use: Soup, pie, or roasted in wedges with chilli.

marrow.store: Somewhere cool and dry for a few weeks.
marrow.preserve: Marrow and ginger jam, or chutney.

melon.store: Ripen at room temperature, then chill before eating.

cucamelon.store: In the fridge for a week.
cucamelon.use: Raw as a snack, or in a gin and tonic.

tomatillo.store: In their husks in the fridge for a couple of weeks.

edamame.store: In the pod in the fridge for a couple of days.
edamame.preserve: Blanch in the pod and freeze.
edamame.use: Boiled in salted water and eaten from the pod.

mangetout.store: In the fridge for a few days.
mangetout.preserve: Blanch for a minute and freeze.
mangetout.use: Raw, or stir-fried for a minute.

watercress.store: Stems in water in the fridge for a couple of days.
watercress.use: Peppery in salads, or watercress soup.

land-cress.store: In a bag in the fridge for a few days.
land-cress.use: Like watercress, in salads and sandwiches.

endive.store: In the fridge for a week.
endive.use: Bitter and crisp: with a sharp dressing, or braised.

chicory.store: In the fridge, in the dark, for a week.
chicory.use: Leaves as scoops for dips, or braised with orange.

winter-purslane.store: In a bag in the fridge for a couple of days.

oriental-greens.store: In a bag in the fridge for a few days.
oriental-greens.use: In salads young, stir-fried when bigger.

mibuna.store: In a bag in the fridge for a few days.
mibuna.use: Mild and mustardy, in salads or soups.

perpetual-spinach.store: In the fridge for a few days.

new-zealand-spinach.store: In the fridge for a couple of days.

daikon.store: In the fridge for a couple of weeks.
daikon.use: Grated raw, or simmered in broth.

elephant-garlic.store: Dry, then keep somewhere cool and airy for months.
elephant-garlic.preserve: Roast whole and freeze the cloves.

welsh-onion.store: Pick as needed; in a glass of water in the fridge for a week.
welsh-onion.use: Like spring onions, raw or cooked.

chinese-cabbage.store: In the fridge for a couple of weeks.
chinese-cabbage.use: Shredded raw, or in stir-fries and soups.

cardoon.store: In the fridge for a few days.
cardoon.use: Stems peeled, boiled, then baked with cheese.

sea-kale.store: In the fridge for a day or two.

summer-squash.store: In the fridge for up to a week.
summer-squash.use: Like courgette: griddled, roasted or raw.

okra.store: In a paper bag in the fridge for a few days.
okra.use: Fried hot and fast, or in a gumbo.

asparagus-pea.store: In the fridge for a day or two; pick them small.
asparagus-pea.use: Steamed whole for a couple of minutes.

borlotti-bean.store: Fresh in the pod for a few days; dried in a jar for a year.
borlotti-bean.preserve: Dry the beans on the plant, then shell and keep in jars.
borlotti-bean.use: Simmered with garlic and sage, or in minestrone.

scorzonera.store: Leave in the ground and lift as needed.
scorzonera.use: Peeled, boiled and fried in butter.

cima-di-rapa.store: In the fridge for a couple of days.

cavolo-nero.store: Pick leaves as needed; in the fridge for five days.
cavolo-nero.use: In ribollita, or with pasta and garlic.

savoy-cabbage.store: Whole heads keep for weeks somewhere cold.
savoy-cabbage.use: Shredded and buttered, or stuffed leaves.

garden-cress.store: Cut as needed; it keeps a day or two.

hamburg-parsley.store: Leave in the ground, or keep in damp sand.
hamburg-parsley.use: Roasted like parsnip; the leaves like parsley.

romanesco.store: In the fridge for up to a week.

orache.store: In the fridge for a day or two.
orache.use: Young leaves in salads, older ones cooked like spinach.

shungiku.store: In the fridge for a couple of days.
shungiku.use: Young leaves raw, or in hotpots and soups.

kai-lan.store: Wrapped in the fridge for three or four days.
kai-lan.preserve: Blanch and freeze, though it’s best fresh.
kai-lan.use: Steamed whole with oyster sauce, or stir-fried with garlic and ginger.

komatsuna.store: In a bag in the fridge for three or four days.
komatsuna.preserve: Best eaten fresh; cooked, it freezes for soups.
komatsuna.use: Raw when small, or wilted into noodles and soups.

tatsoi.store: In a bag in the fridge for three or four days.
tatsoi.use: Small leaves in salads; whole rosettes stir-fried with garlic.

choy-sum.store: Wrapped in the fridge for two or three days.
choy-sum.use: Blanched and dressed with oyster sauce, or stir-fried.

collards.store: In a bag in the fridge for four or five days.
collards.preserve: Blanch the shredded leaves and freeze.
collards.use: Shredded and braised slowly with onion and a little bacon.

red-cabbage.store: Whole heads keep for weeks somewhere cool; cut ones in the fridge.
red-cabbage.preserve: Pickle it, or braise it and freeze.
red-cabbage.use: Braised with apple and vinegar, or shredded raw into slaw.

good-king-henry.store: In a bag in the fridge for a day or two.
good-king-henry.preserve: Blanch the leaves and freeze, as spinach.
good-king-henry.use: Shoots steamed and buttered; leaves cooked as spinach.

skirret.store: Leave in the ground and lift as needed; lifted roots keep a few days in the fridge.
skirret.preserve: They keep best in the ground over winter.
skirret.use: Scrubbed, not peeled, and roasted or sautéed in butter.

oca.store: Somewhere cool and dark for a few months.
oca.preserve: They keep well stored; a few days in the sun makes them sweeter.
oca.use: Roasted like small potatoes, or raw in salads: lemony and crisp.

yacon.store: Somewhere cool for weeks; they get sweeter as they sit.
yacon.preserve: Keeps well stored; or slice and dry.
yacon.use: Raw and crisp like a sweet apple, peeled, in salads.

chinese-artichoke.store: Leave them in the ground; lifted, a day or two in the fridge.
chinese-artichoke.use: Scrubbed and sautéed briefly in butter: crisp and nutty.

summer-purslane.store: In a bag in the fridge for two days.
summer-purslane.use: Raw in salads with tomato, or in a Middle Eastern salad with bread.

amaranth.store: In a bag in the fridge for two days.
amaranth.use: Wilted with garlic, onion and chilli, as callaloo.

malabar-spinach.store: In a bag in the fridge for two or three days.
malabar-spinach.use: Leaves raw in salad, or stirred into curries and soups, where it thickens a little.

celtuce.store: Stems in the fridge for a week; leaves a couple of days.
celtuce.use: The peeled stem sliced thin and stir-fried, or raw like cucumber.

agretti.store: In a bag in the fridge for two or three days.
agretti.use: Blanched for a minute and dressed with olive oil and lemon.

ice-plant.store: In a box in the fridge for a few days.
ice-plant.use: Raw in salads, for its crunch and saltiness.

buckshorn-plantain.store: In a bag in the fridge for a few days.

chickpea.store: Green ones in the fridge for a few days; dried ones in a jar for a year.
chickpea.preserve: Dry them on the plant, then shell and store.
chickpea.use: Green ones roasted in the pod with salt; dried ones soaked and simmered.

yardlong-bean.store: In a bag in the fridge for four or five days.
yardlong-bean.use: Cut into lengths and stir-fried with garlic and chilli.

quinoa.store: Dry and clean, in a jar for a year.
quinoa.preserve: Dry the heads somewhere airy, then rub out the seeds.
quinoa.use: Rinsed well, then simmered for 15 minutes; young leaves as spinach.

tree-spinach.store: In a bag in the fridge for a day or two.
tree-spinach.use: Young shoots raw for their colour; older leaves cooked as spinach.

wasabi.store: Wrap the rhizome in damp paper in the fridge for a couple of weeks.
wasabi.preserve: Grate only what you need: the heat fades in minutes.
wasabi.use: Grated fresh on a fine grater with sushi or steak; leaves in salads.

walking-onion.store: Leaves in the fridge for a few days; top bulbs somewhere cool for months.
walking-onion.use: Leaves as spring onions; bulbs whole in stews or pickled.

babington-leek.store: In the fridge for a week.
babington-leek.use: As leeks: in soups, or sweated in butter.

burdock.store: Wrapped in damp paper in the fridge for a week or two.
burdock.preserve: Keeps in damp sand somewhere cool.
burdock.use: Scraped, cut into matchsticks and braised with carrot, soy and sesame.

perennial-broccoli.store: In the fridge for three or four days.
perennial-broccoli.use: Steamed briefly, with butter or a little anchovy.

samphire.store: Wrapped in damp paper in the fridge for a few days.
samphire.use: Blanched for a minute and buttered, with fish.

achocha.store: In the fridge for a week.
achocha.use: Young ones raw like cucumber; older ones seeded and stir-fried like peppers.

sea-beet.store: In a bag in the fridge for a few days.
sea-beet.use: Cooked as spinach, with butter and nutmeg.

wild-rocket.store: In a bag in the fridge for two days.
wild-rocket.preserve: Best eaten fresh; or blitz into pesto and freeze.
wild-rocket.use: Raw on pizza, in salads, or with pasta and lemon.

texsel-greens.store: In a bag in the fridge for two or three days.
texsel-greens.use: Raw when young, or wilted like spinach with a hint of garlic.

habanero.store: In the fridge for a week or two.
habanero.preserve: Freeze whole, dry them, or make hot sauce.
habanero.use: A sliver at a time: in salsas, curries and hot sauce.

watermelon.store: Whole at room temperature for a week; cut, in the fridge.
watermelon.use: Cold in wedges, or with feta and mint.

perennial-kale.store: In a bag in the fridge for four or five days.
perennial-kale.use: As kale: stripped from the stalks and cooked quickly, or in soups.

turkish-rocket.store: In the fridge for a few days.
turkish-rocket.use: The buds steamed like sprouting broccoli; young leaves wilted.

caucasian-spinach.store: In a bag in the fridge for a day or two.
caucasian-spinach.use: Shoots steamed; leaves cooked as spinach.

mashua.store: Somewhere cool and dark for a few months.
mashua.use: Roasted: peppery raw, milder and sweet when cooked.

chervil-root.store: In sand somewhere cool for months.
chervil-root.preserve: They keep well stored, and get sweeter.
chervil-root.use: Roasted or boiled: floury and chestnut-sweet.

spigarello.store: In a bag in the fridge for four days.
spigarello.use: Sautéed with garlic, chilli and olive oil, with pasta.

ulluco.store: Somewhere cool and dark for months.
ulluco.use: Boiled or roasted; they stay crisp, like new potatoes with a beetroot note.

strawberry-spinach.store: In a bag in the fridge for a day or two.
strawberry-spinach.use: Leaves in salads or wilted; berries scattered over a salad.

lentil.store: Dried, in a jar for a year or more.
lentil.preserve: Dry them in the pod, then shell.
lentil.use: Simmered for dal or soup: no soaking needed.

walking-stick-kale.store: In a bag in the fridge for four or five days.
walking-stick-kale.use: As kale or cabbage: shredded and quickly cooked.

chinese-yam.store: Bulbils and roots somewhere cool for weeks.
chinese-yam.use: Bulbils roasted like tiny potatoes; the root grated raw, Japanese style.

bitter-melon.store: In the fridge for a few days.
bitter-melon.use: Sliced thin, salted to calm the bitterness, then stir-fried with egg.

garden-huckleberry.store: In the fridge for a few days.
garden-huckleberry.preserve: Freeze, or make jam with lemon.
garden-huckleberry.use: Cooked with sugar and lemon in pies and jam: bland raw.

pepino.store: At room temperature until fragrant, then in the fridge.
pepino.use: Peeled and sliced, like a cross of melon and cucumber.

luffa.store: Young ones in the fridge for a few days.
luffa.preserve: Dry the old ones whole for bath sponges.
luffa.use: Young fruit peeled and stir-fried, like courgette.

myoga.store: Wrapped in the fridge for a week.
myoga.preserve: Slice thin and pickle in rice vinegar.
myoga.use: Sliced very thin over tofu, noodles or salad.
